cues: Tongue tip on the ridge of the mouth, touching the back of the top front teeth. It stays there the whole time.
The exhale is forceful and audible. Through the mouth, around the tongue.
asc:breath.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
asc:breath.summary: Four in through the nose, seven held, eight out through the mouth. Four rounds.
asc:breath.why: One of the two you already trust. The long forced exhale is doing the work: emptying the lungs further than a resting breath does means the next inhale arrives without you having to pull for it, and the ratio pushes you further toward the out-breath than any normal breathing pattern goes. Four rounds is the whole dose. It is not a technique that rewards doing more of it.

cues: Two inhales, the second stacked straight on top of the first. Fill the lungs.
Then one long, unhurried exhale. Let it be longer than feels necessary.
Two or three rounds. It works or it does not within about twenty seconds.
asc:breath.name: The Physiological Sigh

phases.note: Long, and all the way out.

asc:breath.summary: Two inhales stacked, then one long exhale. Two or three times, and it is done.
asc:breath.why: The other one you already trust, and the fastest thing on this page. The second inhale reinflates the parts of the lungs the first one did not reach, so the long exhale that follows can offload far more than a single breath could. Two or three is genuinely all of it — this is the one you can do in a conversation, in a queue, in the ninety seconds before something you are dreading.

cues: One big inhale, then one extra inhale on top — squeezing in the extra air.
Both through the nose, if you can.
asc:breath.name: Another Physiological Sigh
asc:breath.summary: The same shape, both breaths through the nose, the second one squeezed in.
asc:breath.why:
A naturally occurring pattern. It is what the body does on its own as you fall asleep, and what it does when you have been crying — the double-inhale hitch is the body downshifting without being asked. That means it can be run deliberately: you are not learning a new trick, you are triggering something already installed.

Damian has not used this variant much. It differs from the one above only in that the second inhale is a genuine squeeze rather than a stack, and both go through the nose if the nose will allow it.

cues: Four to five seconds a side. Pick one count and keep it.
Through the nose on the way in. Slowly on the way out.
At least four rounds. It takes a couple before it starts working.
asc:breath.name: Box Breathing
asc:breath.summary: In for five, hold for five, out for five. Four rounds, at least.
asc:breath.why:
Used by Navy SEALs, Olympic athletes and other people whose job is to stay level in conditions that do not encourage it. Its value is not that it is relaxing — it is that it is boring and countable, and something boring and countable is exactly what a mind running too fast can be given to hold.

Written here as three sides: in, hold, out. Some versions add a fourth — a hold after the exhale, same count — which is where the name comes from. If you want that version, edit this technique and add a hold-after-exhale phase; nothing else has to change.

cues: Inhale for the count, exhale for the same count. One pair per round.
Do not stop at the end. Go straight into the thing you came to do.
asc:breath.name: Vortex Breath
asc:breath.summary: Five descending rounds — 13, 8, 5, 3, 2 — and then you begin.
asc:breath.why:
A ladder rather than a loop. Each round is one inhale and one exhale of the same count, and the counts fall away underneath you: thirteen, eight, five, three, two. By the last pair the breath has become short and the attention has become narrow, which is the point — this is a doorway, not a destination.

Meant for inner growth and mental focus. Run it and then move straight on to whatever mental or spiritual work you sat down for. From the bottom of the ladder a meditative state is very close.

asc:eft.blurb: For when the body has decided something is wrong and will not be talked out of it.
asc:eft.closing: Stop. Take one long breath out. Then read the number again — and be honest if it has not moved much, because a second pass on an honest six does more than a first pass on a pretend three.
asc:eft.name: Anxiety

reframe.phrase: I am safe in this moment.
My body is beginning to settle.
I can feel my breath again.
Whatever is coming, I will meet it then, not now.
I am allowed to be calm.
There is more room in my chest.
I am okay right now.
I am here, and I am okay.

round1.phrase: All this anxiety.
This tightness in my chest.
My body thinks something is coming.
And I cannot argue it out of that.
It has been sitting here all day.
I cannot get a full breath.
I am so tired of feeling like this.
All of this anxiety.

round2.phrase: But this is my body trying to protect me.
It is doing the only thing it knows how to do.
It is not wrong about danger, it is just early.
I am in a room, and I am safe in it.
Nothing is happening right this second.
I am allowed to put some of this down.
Some of it can leave now.
It is already less than it was.

setup: Even though I feel all this anxiety in my body right now, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though my body has decided something is wrong and I cannot reason it out of that, I accept how I feel.
Even though I do not know exactly what this is about, I am safe enough to feel it.

asc:eft.blurb: For too much at once, and no obvious thing to put down.
asc:eft.closing: Before you get up: name the single next action out loud. Stress usually comes back the moment the list becomes abstract again.
asc:eft.name: Stress

reframe.phrase: One thing at a time.
I know what the next thing is.
My shoulders are down.
I am steady enough to start.
I am allowed to work at a human pace.
The rest can wait its turn.
I have handled more than this before.
One thing at a time, and I am fine.

round1.phrase: There is too much.
All of it, at the same time.
And none of it can wait.
My shoulders have been up all day.
I am running and not arriving.
I cannot think clearly enough to prioritise.
All this pressure.
All of this stress.

round2.phrase: But it is not all happening right now.
Most of it is happening in my head, in advance.
Only one thing can be done at a time anyway.
I do not have to hold all of it to do the next bit.
My shoulders can come down.
I am allowed to set some of it down while I work.
It will still be there. I do not need to carry it.
I can loosen my grip a little.

setup: Even though there is too much and I cannot see the end of it, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I am carrying all of this at the same time, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I do not have room for any of this, I choose to be on my own side about it.

asc:eft.blurb: For a specific thing you are afraid of, named out loud.
asc:eft.closing: If the number barely moved, the fear underneath is probably a different one. Run it again with the more embarrassing sentence.
asc:eft.name: Fear

reframe.phrase: I can be afraid and do it anyway.
That is the only kind of brave there is.
I am more capable than I feel right now.
Whatever happens, I will handle it.
I have handled every other thing I was sure I could not.
I am steadier than this fear says.
I can walk toward it.
I am ready enough.

round1.phrase: This fear.
I know exactly what I am afraid of.
And I have already watched it go wrong in my head.
Several times.
My body reacts as if it has already happened.
I do not want to face it.
All of this fear.
This fear, right here.

round2.phrase: But rehearsing it is not the same as it happening.
I have been wrong about how things would go before.
Often, in fact.
And if the worst did happen, I would still be here.
Fear is not a prediction.
It is a warning that has not checked its facts.
I can be afraid and still go.
Some of this can go now.

setup: Even though I am afraid of this, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though part of me is certain it will go badly, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I would rather not look at this directly, I am willing to look at it now.

asc:eft.blurb: For the loop that feels like problem-solving and is not.
asc:eft.closing: The loop restarts fastest with nothing else to do. Go straight into something with your hands in it.
asc:eft.name: Overthinking

reframe.phrase: My mind can rest.
I do not have to solve this tonight.
I trust myself to know when it is time to decide.
Uncertainty is survivable.
I can leave the question open.
My head is quieter.
I am allowed to think about something else.
Quiet.

round1.phrase: Round and round.
The same loop, again.
I have already thought this exact thought today.
It feels like I am working on it.
But nothing new has arrived in hours.
I cannot put it down.
My head is exhausting.
All this thinking.

round2.phrase: But thinking is not the same as deciding.
And I already know what I think.
The loop is not looking for an answer.
It is looking for a guarantee, and there is not one.
I am allowed to act without being certain.
I can let the question sit unanswered.
The loop can slow down.
It is already quieter.

setup: Even though my mind will not stop turning this over, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I have thought about this a hundred times and gained nothing, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though thinking feels safer than deciding, I accept where I am.

asc:eft.blurb: For the voice that arrives exactly when you are about to try.
asc:eft.closing: Open the Evidence Journal afterwards. Doubt argues with feelings and loses to records.
asc:eft.name: Self-Doubt

reframe.phrase: I am allowed to take up this space.
I do not need to be certain to begin.
I have evidence, and I have been collecting it.
I know more than I give myself credit for.
Being new at something is not being a fraud.
I can do this badly first and well later.
I trust myself enough to start.
I am enough for this.

round1.phrase: This doubt.
Who am I to be doing this.
Someone else would do it better.
They are going to see through me.
I have got away with it so far.
All this doubt.
It arrives right when I am about to start.
Every time.

round2.phrase: But the timing gives it away.
It never shows up when I am doing nothing.
It shows up when I am about to be seen.
That is not an assessment. That is a reflex.
And I have done things I doubted I could do.
More than once.
The doubt was wrong then too.
Some of this can go.

setup: Even though I do not think I am good enough for this, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though part of me is certain I will be found out, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I doubt myself, I am willing to act anyway.

asc:eft.blurb: For the thing that has been on the list for eleven days.
asc:eft.closing: Do not close this and plan. Open Unstick, fill the last box only, and go.
asc:eft.name: Procrastination

reframe.phrase: I can start without wanting to.
Motivation comes after, not before.
I only have to do the first small piece.
Badly done is further along than not started.
I am allowed to do this imperfectly.
The relief afterwards is worth more than the comfort now.
I am starting today.
I am starting now.

round1.phrase: I am still not doing it.
It has been on the list for days.
It gets heavier every day I leave it.
And the heavier it gets, the less I want to start.
I keep doing everything except this.
I am annoyed at myself.
Which has not helped once.
All this avoidance.

round2.phrase: But this is not laziness.
There is a feeling under it I have not looked at.
Maybe it is that I might do it badly.
Maybe it is just that it is boring and I resent it.
Either way, avoiding it costs more than doing it.
And it is smaller than it has become in my head.
I could do five minutes of it.
Five minutes is not a decision.

setup: Even though I am still not doing this, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I do not fully know why I am avoiding it, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I have made this harder by leaving it, I am not going to punish myself for it now.

asc:eft.blurb: For the thing you would not want said out loud. Go gently here.
asc:eft.closing: This one often needs more than one pass, and it is normal for the number to move slowly. Stop while you still feel steady. There is no prize for finishing.
asc:eft.name: Shame

reframe.phrase: I am a person who did a thing, not a bad thing that walks around.
I can hold this without being crushed by it.
I have already changed since then.
I am allowed to be human about it.
I can be honest and still be okay.
I am worthy of my own kindness.
I forgive myself for this.
I am still worth something.

round1.phrase: This shame.
I do not want anyone to know this about me.
It is heavy and it is old.
It does not say I did something bad.
It says I am something bad.
I want to disappear when I think about it.
All of this shame.
All of it.

round2.phrase: But shame only survives in the dark.
And I have just said it, here, to myself.
That already changes something.
What I did and what I am are different things.
I was doing what I knew how to do at the time.
I would forgive anyone else for this.
I am allowed the same.
It can weigh less than it did.

setup: Even though I feel this shame, and I do not want to look at it, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though part of me believes I am the problem, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though this is hard to say even alone, I am willing to say it.

asc:eft.blurb: For anger that has nowhere to go. It does not need justifying first.
asc:eft.closing: If this leaves you flat rather than calm, that is usually the hurt arriving. Grounding, or the Inner Work Journal, is the better next step than another round.
asc:eft.name: Anger

reframe.phrase: I can feel this without being run by it.
My anger tells me a boundary was crossed.
I have heard it. It can stand down now.
I choose what I do next.
My hands are loose.
My jaw is loose.
I am cooler than I was.
I am in charge of this, not the other way round.

round1.phrase: This anger.
I am furious.
And I am right to be.
It was not fair.
It is sitting in my jaw and my hands.
And there is nowhere to put it.
All this anger.
All of it, with nowhere to go.

round2.phrase: But it does not have to be justified to be released.
I can be right and still put it down.
Carrying it is not the same as being taken seriously.
It is costing me more than it is costing them.
There is usually hurt underneath this.
And the hurt is allowed too.
My jaw can unclench.
Some of this heat can leave.

setup: Even though I am furious about this, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I have nowhere to put this anger, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though part of me thinks I should not feel this strongly, I am allowed to.

asc:eft.blurb: Before the thing. Not a session for after it has gone badly.
asc:eft.closing: Stand up before you finish. This one does not hold if you do it slumped.
asc:eft.name: Confidence

reframe.phrase: I am allowed to be seen.
I have something worth saying.
I am calm in my own body.
I do not need everyone to approve.
I trust myself in the room.
I can take up space.
I am ready enough, and ready enough is ready.
I have got this.

round1.phrase: I do not feel ready.
I want to make myself smaller.
I am worried about how I will come across.
I am watching myself from outside.
That is not helping.
All this self-consciousness.
I would rather not be seen.
All of it.

round2.phrase: But confidence is not a feeling I have to wait for.
It is what happens after doing the thing, not before.
Nobody watching me is watching as closely as I am.
I can stand up straight even feeling like this.
I have prepared. I know what I am doing.
I can let myself take up the room I am in.
Some of this can go.
I am steadier than a minute ago.

setup: Even though I do not feel ready for this, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though part of me wants to shrink, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I do not feel confident, I choose to act like someone who is.

asc:eft.blurb: For a body that will not switch off. Run it in bed, in the dark.
asc:eft.closing: Do not check the number. Go straight into 4-7-8 and stop there.
asc:eft.name: Sleep

reframe.phrase: It is safe to let go now.
There is nothing I need to be awake for.
My body is heavy and warm.
My breathing is slowing on its own.
Tomorrow will be handled tomorrow.
I am allowed to rest.
I am sinking.
Letting go.

round1.phrase: I am still awake.
My body will not switch off.
My mind started the moment it got quiet.
Tomorrow is going to be harder because of this.
Which is not making me sleepier.
I am wired and I am tired.
All this restlessness.
Still awake.

round2.phrase: But nothing has to be solved tonight.
Nothing on that list is a night-time problem.
Lying still and resting counts for something.
Sleep is not a test I can fail.
My body knows how to do this.
It has done it thousands of times.
I can let it get heavy.
Heavier already.

setup: Even though my body will not switch off, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though my mind starts up the moment it goes quiet, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though I am frustrated about being awake, I am going to be gentle about it.

asc:eft.blurb: For the tightness around money, opportunity, and having enough.
asc:eft.closing: Then do one concrete thing about it — a number checked, an email sent. This one goes stale fastest if it stays a feeling.
asc:eft.name: Abundance

reframe.phrase: There is enough, and I am allowed some of it.
I am allowed to want more than I have.
Opportunities are for people like me.
I can receive without flinching.
I am building something.
I am not behind. I am on my own line.
I am open to good things arriving.
There is enough.

round1.phrase: This tightness about money.
The fear that there will not be enough.
I feel behind everyone else.
It always seems to come to other people more easily.
I am bracing for something to go wrong.
It is hard to want things out loud.
All this scarcity.
All of this.

round2.phrase: But bracing has never once made more arrive.
Fear makes me small, and small does not earn.
This is mostly an old inheritance, not a forecast.
I have had enough before and did not notice.
Wanting something is not greedy.
Other people having things does not take from me.
I can loosen this grip.
A little looser already.

setup: Even though I am afraid there will not be enough, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I feel behind, I accept myself and where I am.
Even though part of me does not believe good things are for me, I am open to being wrong.

asc:eft.blurb: The deepest one here. Not about a situation — about the baseline.
asc:eft.closing: This is the one that moves in tenths, not points. Do not judge it by one session — the Evidence Journal is where this argument is actually won, over months.
asc:eft.name: Self-Worth

reframe.phrase: I am worth something as I am.
Not because of what I produced.
I am allowed to rest without having earned it.
I am allowed to take up room.
I can be kind to myself on a bad day.
I would want this for anyone else. I am included.
I matter.
I matter, and that is not conditional.

round1.phrase: This feeling that I am not worth much.
That I have to earn my place, every day.
That I am only as good as what I produced this week.
I cannot rest without feeling I am getting away with something.
It is not about today. It is much older than today.
I have believed it for a long time.
All of this.
All of this, and how tired it makes me.

round2.phrase: But I learned this. It did not come with me.
Someone taught it, and I believed them.
I do not apply this rule to anyone else.
I would never say this to a person I loved.
Worth is not a wage.
It is not something I have to keep re-earning.
I can loosen my hold on this.
Just a little, for now.

setup: Even though somewhere I believe I am not worth much, I deeply and completely accept myself.
Even though I have to earn my place before I am allowed to rest, I accept myself and how I feel.
Even though this one is old and I cannot argue it away, I am willing to loosen it.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Tap it with the four fingers of the other hand. This is the setup point — you only use it while saying the setup statement.
asc:eftpoints.name: Karate chop
asc:eftpoints.where: The fleshy outer edge of the hand, below the little finger.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Two fingers, firm but gentle, about seven taps. Either side, or both at once.
asc:eftpoints.name: Eyebrow
asc:eftpoints.where: Where the eyebrow begins, just above and to one side of the bridge of the nose.

asc:eftpoints.cue: On the bone, not on the soft tissue. Two fingers.
asc:eftpoints.name: Side of the eye
asc:eftpoints.where: On the bone at the outside corner of the eye.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Light here. It is a thin bone and a tender spot.
asc:eftpoints.name: Under the eye
asc:eftpoints.where: On the bone under the eye, roughly below the pupil.

asc:eftpoints.cue: One or two fingers. A small target, so slow down.
asc:eftpoints.name: Under the nose
asc:eftpoints.where: The small hollow between the nose and the top lip.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Two fingers in the crease itself, not on the point of the chin.
asc:eftpoints.name: Chin
asc:eftpoints.where: The crease between the bottom lip and the chin.

asc:eftpoints.cue: You can tap this one with a loose fist across both sides at once. Often the strongest point of the round.
asc:eftpoints.name: Collarbone
asc:eftpoints.where: Just below the inner end of the collarbone, about an inch down and an inch out from the notch at the base of the throat.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Flat fingers, or the whole hand. Reach across the body.
asc:eftpoints.name: Under the arm
asc:eftpoints.where: About four inches below the armpit, level with a bra strap.

asc:eftpoints.cue: Fingers spread, tapping in a small circle. This closes the round.
asc:eftpoints.name: Top of the head
asc:eftpoints.where: The crown, the centre of the top of the head.

steps: Sit with both feet flat. Let your weight actually land in the chair.
Picture a root running down from the base of your spine, through the floor, through everything under the floor, into the ground.
Let it go further than feels reasonable. Deep, and thick, and slow.
On each exhale, send whatever you are carrying down the root.
On each inhale, draw something steady and cool back up.
Stay until your body feels heavier than when you started. That heaviness is the whole point.
asc:energy.summary: Roots down from the base of the spine into the ground, and weight arriving with them.
asc:energy.title: Grounding visualization

steps: Stand with your feet about hip width apart. Bare feet if you can.
Press down through all four corners of each foot — big toe, little toe, inner heel, outer heel.
Rock very slightly forward and back until you find the place where you are genuinely balanced.
Soften your knees. A locked knee cannot ground.
Breathe down into your feet for ten breaths, as though the breath went that far.
asc:energy.summary: Standing, barefoot if possible. Weight, contact, and nothing else.
asc:energy.title: Rooting

steps: Get outside. A garden, a park, a verge — it does not have to be beautiful.
If you can, put your bare feet on grass or earth.
Name five things you can see, then four you can hear, then three you can feel.
Do not narrate. If a thought about your day arrives, go back to naming.
Ten to fifteen minutes. Longer is better and shorter still works.
asc:energy.summary: Outside, on actual ground, with your attention on the outside rather than the inside.
asc:energy.title: Nature grounding

steps: Sit or lie down. Close your eyes if that is comfortable.
Start at your feet. What is actually there — temperature, pressure, tingling, nothing at all?
Move up slowly: shins, knees, thighs, hips, belly, chest, hands, arms, shoulders, neck, face.
Do not fix anything. You are taking an inventory, not doing repairs.
When you reach the top, notice the whole body at once for a few breaths.
asc:energy.summary: A scan from the feet up, with no attempt to change anything on the way.
asc:energy.title: Body awareness

steps: Stand up. Shake your hands out for a few seconds.
Starting at the top of your head, sweep your hands down over your body a few inches away from it — head, face, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, legs.
At the end of each sweep, flick your hands away from you.
Do the back of your body too, as far as you can reach.
Three full passes. Then stand still and notice what changed.
asc:energy.summary: A sweep from head to feet, brushing off what is not yours.
asc:energy.title: Energy clearing

steps: Sit comfortably. Take three slow breaths.
Picture a clear light entering at the top of your head.
Let it move down slowly, filling you like water fills a glass — head, throat, chest, belly, hips, legs.
Anything cloudy or heavy it meets, it carries down with it.
It leaves through the soles of your feet and goes into the ground, where it is composted rather than stored.
Repeat until the light runs clear.
asc:energy.summary: Light entering at the crown, moving down, and taking the residue out through the feet.
asc:energy.title: Cleansing visualization

steps: Stand with your feet planted.
Take a normal breath in through the nose.
Exhale sharply through the mouth with a sound — a "ha" from the belly, not the throat.
Ten of these. Let them be loud. Muffling it defeats the point.
Then stop completely and stand still for thirty seconds without moving.
asc:energy.summary: Sharp exhales through the mouth. Loud, and slightly undignified.
asc:energy.title: Breath clearing

steps: Get in. Stand under the water for a few seconds before doing anything else.
As the water runs over your head and shoulders, decide it is carrying the day off you.
Name what you are letting go of. Out loud if you are alone, silently if you are not.
Turn slowly so the water reaches your back and neck.
Before you get out, take one breath and name what you want to walk out with instead.
asc:energy.summary: The one that needs no extra time in the day, because you were going to shower anyway.
asc:energy.title: Shower cleansing ritual

steps: Stand or sit. Feet on the floor.
Picture a layer about a hand's width off your skin, covering you completely — including underneath your feet and above your head.
Give it a texture. Mirrored, or woven, or simply solid; whatever you can actually picture.
Set the rule: what is mine passes through, what is not mine does not.
Check it once during the day. Repair anything thin.
asc:energy.summary: A worn shield rather than a wall. Built in the morning, checked in the evening.
asc:energy.title: Energy shielding

steps: One breath in.
On the way out, picture a bubble expanding to about an arm's length around you.
Make it a colour. The colour matters less than being definite about it.
Say, internally: this is mine, and it holds.
Walk in.
asc:energy.summary: The fast one, for a doorway or a car park before you go in.
asc:energy.title: Bubble visualization

steps: Name the person or situation you have been leaking into.
Write, in one plain sentence, the limit you actually want. Not the diplomatic version — the true one.
Ask: is this a limit on THEM, or a limit on what I will do? Rewrite it as the second one, because that is the only kind you can enforce.
Decide what you will do the next time it is crossed.
Say the sentence out loud once, to nobody. It has to have been said somewhere before it can be said to them.
asc:energy.summary: The unmystical one. Naming a limit is what makes it exist.
asc:energy.title: Boundaries

steps: Sit somewhere you will not be interrupted. Bring the person to mind without arguing with them.
Notice where a cord seems to run between you — usually the belly, the chest, or the throat.
Look at what it is made of, and how long it has been there.
Say what you actually want to say. All of it.
Then release it — cut it, untie it, let it dissolve. Whichever you can genuinely picture.
Close the place it was attached with a hand there and a breath. Sit for a minute afterwards; this one leaves a gap.
asc:energy.summary: For a relationship you are still carrying around after it is over.
asc:energy.title: Cord visualization

steps: Sit upright. Three settling breaths.
Base of the spine — red. Am I safe? Breathe there until it feels present.
Below the navel — orange. Am I able to feel and to want?
Solar plexus — yellow. Do I have any power here?
Heart — green. Am I open, or closed?
Throat — blue. Am I saying what is true?
Brow — indigo. Can I see clearly?
Crown — violet or white. Am I connected to anything larger?
End by drawing attention back down to the base. Never finish this one at the top.
asc:energy.summary: Seven centres, bottom to top, a minute or two each.
asc:energy.title: Chakra practices

steps: Rub your palms together until they are warm.
Place both hands over your eyes. Stay for two or three minutes.
Move to the sides of the head, then the back of the head, then the throat.
Then the heart, then the solar plexus, then the belly.
No pressure. The hand rests; the attention does the work.
Finish with both hands on the belly and a few slow breaths.
asc:energy.summary: Hands on, one position at a time, with attention rather than pressure.
asc:energy.title: Reiki

steps: Sit upright, feet flat, tongue resting on the roof of the mouth.
On the inhale, draw attention from the base of the spine up the back to the crown.
On the exhale, let it fall down the front of the body to the base again.
Keep the circle turning at the pace of the breath, not faster.
Twenty circuits. If you lose it, pick it up from wherever you are.
asc:energy.summary: A loop up the back and down the front, moved by the breath.
asc:energy.title: Energy circulation

steps: Stand with feet shoulder width, knees soft, weight in the middle of the feet.
Raise your hands to chest height, palms facing each other, about a foot apart.
Move them slowly together and apart. Look for resistance between them.
When you find it, stay at that distance and breathe.
Then slowly lower your hands to your belly and stand still for a minute.
asc:energy.summary: Standing, knees soft, hands moving slowly with something between them.
asc:energy.title: Qi practices

steps: Sit with your eyes closed. Settle for a minute.
Bring your attention to the space immediately around your body, rather than to your body.
Notice size — does it feel close in, or wide? Even, or lopsided?
Notice colour, if a colour arrives. Do not force one.
Where it feels thin, breathe into that side until it evens out.
Finish by drawing the whole field in slightly, to about arm's length.
asc:energy.summary: Looking at the field around you rather than at the body inside it.
asc:energy.title: Aura visualization

steps: Stand up. Start with the hands, then the arms.
Let it spread — shoulders, ribs, hips, legs. Bounce through the knees.
Keep it going for two minutes. It will feel silly around forty seconds. Continue.
Then stop dead and stand completely still with your eyes closed.
Stay still for a full minute. The stillness after is where the change lands.
asc:energy.summary: The fastest state change on this page. Two minutes, whole body.
asc:energy.title: Shaking

steps: Take a normal breath in through the nose.
Hum all the way out, low and steady, until you actually run out.
Find the pitch that buzzes most in your face and chest, and stay there.
Ten breaths.
Then sit quietly for thirty seconds and notice the difference.
asc:energy.summary: A long hum on the out-breath. Vibration in the chest and the face.
asc:energy.title: Humming

steps: Put on one piece of music you like.
Start moving before you have decided how. Any part, any way.
Follow whatever wants to move rather than leading it.
No mirrors, no watching yourself, no correct version of this.
Stop when the track ends and stand still for a moment.
asc:energy.summary: Not exercise. Moving whichever way the body asks, with no sequence.
asc:energy.title: Movement

steps: Somewhere you can be heard without consequence. In the car, if nowhere else.
Take a full breath in.
Make a sound on the way out — a vowel, a sigh, a shout. Not a word.
Let it be genuinely loud at least once.
Five or six of these, then sit in the silence afterwards.
asc:energy.summary: Making a noise on purpose. Loud enough to be slightly embarrassing.
asc:energy.title: Sound

steps: Name the state you are in now, plainly. One word.
Name the state you would rather be in.
Find a real memory of being in the second one. Not a fantasy — a time it actually happened.
Go into it fully: where you were, what you could see, what your body felt like, what you were doing with your hands.
Stay in it for a full minute rather than glancing at it.
Open your eyes still holding it, and do the next thing from there.
asc:energy.summary: Change the channel. Borrow a state you have actually had.
asc:energy.title: State-shift visualization

asc:media:breathmed.description: Count to ten on the exhale, then start again. Losing count is not failure; noticing you lost count is the practice.
asc:media:breathmed.title: Breath counting

asc:media:breathmed.description: Five and a half seconds in, five and a half out, for the whole session. Boring by design.
asc:media:breathmed.title: Coherent breathing

asc:media:breathmed.description: Follow the breath by where it is felt — nostrils, chest, belly — rather than by counting it.
asc:media:breathmed.forWhen: When the breath will not settle
asc:media:breathmed.title: Breath and body

asc:media:breathmed.description: Exhale roughly twice the length of the inhale, held for the whole sit rather than a few rounds.
asc:media:breathmed.title: Extended exhale sit

asc:media:hypnosis.description: Long, slow, and designed not to be finished. Falling asleep partway through is success.
asc:media:hypnosis.title: Sleep induction

asc:media:hypnosis.description: Suggestion work aimed at how you carry yourself rather than at what you believe.
asc:media:hypnosis.title: Confidence installation

asc:media:hypnosis.description: Deepening, then direct suggestion, then a slow return. Do not run this while driving or doing anything else.
asc:media:hypnosis.title: Anxiety release

asc:media:hypnosis.description: The deepest of these, and the one that wants repetition — daily for a few weeks beats occasionally forever.
asc:media:hypnosis.title: Self-worth rewrite

asc:media:hypnosis.description: One habit per session. Two at once and neither lands.
asc:media:hypnosis.forWhen: Installing or removing one specific thing
asc:media:hypnosis.title: Habit change

asc:media:meditation.description: Plain attention on the breath, coming back when it wanders. The default, and the one to build the habit on.
asc:media:meditation.title: Ten-minute sit

asc:media:meditation.description: Feet to crown, region by region. Doubles as a way to fall asleep if you do it lying down, which is either a bug or a feature.
asc:media:meditation.forWhen: When you are living in your head
asc:media:meditation.title: Body scan

asc:media:meditation.description: Label what arrives — thinking, hearing, feeling — and let it go. Gives an overactive mind a job small enough to keep it out of the way.
asc:media:meditation.title: Noting practice

asc:media:meditation.description: Goodwill directed outward in widening circles, starting with yourself, which is usually the hardest one.
asc:media:meditation.forWhen: After a bad day with people
asc:media:meditation.title: Loving-kindness

asc:media:meditation.description: No object at all. Not a beginner practice, and frustrating if you arrive agitated.
asc:media:meditation.forWhen: When you are already fairly settled
asc:media:meditation.title: Open awareness

asc:media:meditation.description: Short enough that there is no excuse. Sit down, close your eyes, follow ten breaths, get up.
asc:media:meditation.title: Two-minute reset

asc:media:visualization.description: Build one place in full detail and return to the same one every time. It gets stronger with repetition, which a new place each session never does.
asc:media:visualization.title: Safe place

asc:media:visualization.description: A day in the life of the person you are becoming, in specifics — what they do first, what they refuse, what their afternoon looks like.
asc:media:visualization.forWhen: When the direction has gone blurry
asc:media:visualization.title: Future self

asc:media:visualization.description: Light moving through the body, resting anywhere that asks for it.
asc:media:visualization.title: Healing light

asc:media:visualization.description: Ten steps down, counted, each one deeper. A doorway practice rather than a destination.
asc:media:visualization.title: The staircase

asc:media:visualization.description: You are the mountain; the weather is the weather. Borrowed from MBSR and worth the fifteen minutes.
asc:media:visualization.title: Mountain

asc:media:walking.description: Ten paces, turn, ten paces back. Attention on the sole of the foot as it lands. Indoors, and slower than feels sensible.
asc:media:walking.title: Slow walking practice

asc:media:walking.description: Normal pace, no headphones, attention on what is actually around you. The loop dies faster walking than sitting.
asc:media:walking.title: Walking outside

asc:media:walking.description: Breathe in for four steps, out for six. The rhythm does most of the work.
asc:media:walking.forWhen: A mind that needs a handle
asc:media:walking.title: Counting steps

asc:media:walking.description: Name one thing you are glad of per street, or per hundred paces. Specific things, not categories.
asc:media:walking.title: Gratitude walk

asc:yoga.description: Every major joint through its full range, in order, from the neck down to the ankles. The one to reach for when you have been at a desk and everything feels short.
asc:yoga.title: Full-body mobility flow

asc:yoga.description: Cat-cow, thread the needle, thoracic rotations. Short, and aimed squarely at where a day of sitting collects.
asc:yoga.title: Spine and shoulders

asc:yoga.description: Low lunges, half splits, pigeon. Slow enough that the hips actually let go rather than bracing.
asc:yoga.title: Hips and hamstrings

asc:yoga.description: Low to the floor and heavily supported the whole way. Child's pose, supported forward fold, legs up the wall. Weight and contact are the active ingredients.
asc:yoga.title: Grounding practice

asc:yoga.description: For the day the anxiety is physical. Long holds, nothing to balance on, nothing to get right.
asc:yoga.title: Anxious body reset

asc:yoga.description: Almost entirely seated and supine. Movement that asks nothing back — for the evening where doing nothing feels worse but doing anything feels impossible.
asc:yoga.title: Gentle practice for a tired body

asc:yoga.description: Four or five shapes, held for minutes each, with cushions doing all the work. Closer to sleep than to exercise, and that is the point.
asc:yoga.title: Supported rest

asc:yoga.description: Sun salutations, standing shapes, one balance. Enough to change your state before the day starts making decisions for you.
asc:yoga.title: Morning wake-up flow

asc:yoga.description: Continuous and warm. For the restlessness that will not be sat still with and has to be spent first.
asc:yoga.title: Active flow

asc:yoga.description: The version that survives a bad morning. Eight minutes, standing, no mat required.
asc:yoga.title: Short morning mobility

asc:yoga.description: Floor shapes held for three to five minutes. Done in dim light, ideally already in what you are sleeping in.
asc:yoga.title: Bedtime wind-down

asc:yoga.description: Long holds where the discomfort is mild and the mind has nowhere to go but the breath. The stillness is the practice, not the shape.
asc:yoga.title: Yin for a wired mind

asc:yoga.description: One shape, ten minutes, against an actual wall. The highest ratio of effect to effort on this page.
asc:yoga.title: Legs up the wall

asc:yoga.description: Quads, hamstrings, calves, chest, lats. Straight after training, while everything is still warm.
asc:yoga.title: Post-workout stretch

asc:yoga.description: For the day after. Gentle range work rather than deep stretching — sore tissue does not want to be pulled on.
asc:yoga.title: Recovery flow

asc:yoga.description: Neck, forearms, hip flexors, upper back. Can be done in normal clothes without lying down.
asc:yoga.title: Desk recovery

asc:yoga.description: Shake first, then be completely still and notice what is left. The stillness afterwards is where the practice actually happens.
asc:yoga.title: Somatic shaking and settling

asc:yoga.description: Move one region at a time and pay attention to it while it moves. For when you have been living several inches above your own body.
asc:yoga.title: Body scan in movement

asc:yoga.description: Very small, very slow movements on the floor, led by curiosity rather than a sequence. Nothing to achieve and no shape to reach.
asc:yoga.title: Slow floor somatics

asc:yoga.description: The transition practice — for the gap between finishing work and being a person again.
asc:yoga.title: Evening unwind

asc:yoga.description: A longer evening session for a day with room in it. Everything, unhurried.
asc:yoga.title: Evening full-body
